name: add_character
description: Log in EVE Online characters via ESI OAuth2. Opens the user's browser at EVE's login page; afterwards the browser shows a neat page listing their characters, where they can log in more characters before clicking Done or closing the tab. Blocks until then and returns every character added, with the scope groups each granted. Every login grants the basic scope group plus scopeGroups: before calling, ask the user what they'll use neat for, including whether they want their corporation's data, and pick groups from list_scope_groups (or use only basic if they don't know). A login replaces each character's access with exactly what it requested, so to add a group to characters already logged in, either pass characterId or list every group they should end up with; list_characters doesn't show a character's current groups, so if you don't know them, pass characterId. If no browser tab opens, the user can open http://127.0.0.1:48211/ themselves while the tool waits. To grant more groups to a character later (e.g. after a tool fails because a scope is missing), pass its characterId: its existing scopes are kept. Check the result's warnings: they say when the user logged in as a different character, or when the character's earlier scope groups couldn't be read and may need granting again. Re-adding a known character refreshes its login.

Also says whether the generator fits the hull and which skills the lighter still needs.

name: get_logistics_overview
description: Start here for any move of ships, cargo or characters. One call gives, for each logged-in character: their account label, whether they're online, where they are (system with its displayed security, and the station or structure they're docked in), their ship, the cynos, bridges and conduits they can use with the hulls for each, the hauling and capital hulls they can fly, when they can next clone jump, whether they can clone jump from where they're docked, and where their jump clones are, and their jump fatigue. It also groups characters by account, flags labels the game contradicts (two characters labelled alike online at once; when one of them logged in within the last minute, it waits about a minute and checks again, since ESI can still show a character who just switched off as online), and warns about unknown accounts. Parts ESI won't give are named per character, not dropped silently.

readyNow.description: true only when the cooldown has passed and they're docked where a clone bay is known to be (jumpFromHere yes)

Totals give the volume to move with ships repackaged or carried assembled, overall and per owner in sources: items in one character's personal hangar can only be hauled by another pilot once its owner gives them over with an item exchange contract. notes.description: replaces the notes of the one character in characterIds: what the user says the character is for or can do. An empty string clears them

renameAccount.description: rename an account label for every character that has it

from.description: the account label in use now

to.description: the new label; renaming onto a label already in use merges the two accounts

account.description: the user's label for the EVE account this character is on; characters with the same label share an account and can't be logged in at the same time; absent means unknown

notes.description: what the user has said about this character

name: update_character_mail
description: Update the read status and/or labels of one of a logged-in EVE Online character's mails. This changes state on EVE's server.

labels.description: replace the mail's label IDs with this set; omit to leave labels unchanged

read.description: mark the mail read (true) or unread (false); omit to leave read status unchanged

name: update_fleet
description: Update a fleet's settings — this changes state on EVE's server.

characterId.description: the character ID to check as -- must have fleet_commander role

isFreeMove.description: whether free-move is enabled; omit to leave unchanged

motd.description: new fleet MOTD in FC-flavoured HTML; omit to leave unchanged

name: validate_trade_hub
description: Measure how good a trade hub is on live ESI data and record the dated result on it: how many of a basket of 24 everyday goods it has for sale (or a basket you give), with its sell and buy order counts, and optionally its public contracts by value with the capital ship groups on offer (the check for a capital market). Works for a saved hub or a new station or structure ID, which it then saves. Run it before relying on a hub whose validation is stale. Writes to ~/.neat/hubs.yaml only.

basket.description: items to check for sale instead of the default basket of 24 everyday goods; quantities are ignored

typeId.description: item type ID; used when name is empty

characterId.description: for a player structure: a logged-in character with docking access; defaults to the one that last read it

contracts.description: also count public contracts starting there by value, and list the capital ship groups on offer; the check for a capital market

hub.description: a saved hub's name or ID, or a new station or structure ID to measure and save

field.description: the field that changed, as a dotted path; absent when a whole entry was added or removed

id.description: the NPC station or structure ID

readVia.description: the character that last read this structure hub's market

tier.description: major (the five NPC hubs), secondary (player structure markets) or lowsec

traits.description: what the hub is good for, in a few words each

missing.description: basket items with no sell order there

stocked.description: items of the basket with at least one sell order at the hub

over10b.description: of those, priced at 10B ISK or more

over1b.description: of those, priced at 1B ISK or more

public.description: public item exchange and auction contracts starting there

shipGroups.description: capital and supercapital ship groups on offer in the priciest contracts
